records.title: KSh 13 billion catalytic funding announced at KDEAP backbone pre-bid session (at least 27,000 km, Multi-Round Reverse Auction)
records.organisation: State Department for ICT and the Digital Economy / ICT Authority (recorded via official LinkedIn post of PS Eng. John Kipchumba Tanui)
claims_extracted: The Government is making available KSh 13 billion to catalyse matching private investment and deliver at least 27,000 km of backbone, middle-mile and cross-border fibre.
Public support will be allocated competitively through a Multi-Round Reverse Auction (MRRA) to mobilise matching private capital.
Since 2022, the private sector has added 24,000 km of fibre and the public sector 17,000 km.

The Communications Authority's April-June 2026 report records 88M mobile subscriptions, 54.9M mobile broadband and 54M mobile money subscriptions; fixed internet connections reached 2.84 million by June 2026, up 32.4 percent, including 1.57 million fibre connections (up 29.7 percent); submarine cables and cross-border links give Kenya approximately 28.95 Tbps of international bandwidth.
Ambition: over eight million fixed broadband connections.
Also present at the pre-bid session was the CEO of the ICT Authority, Mr. Jesse Maruti (per the post).
records.evidence_excerpt: The Government is making available KSh 13 billion to catalyse matching private investment and deliver at least 27,000 km of backbone, middle-mile and cross-border fibre - closing connectivity gaps, strengthening resilience and making it cheaper to connect homes, businesses and public institutions.

records.title: Microsoft wind-down of Nairobi Africa Development Centre; government presses for job protection
records.organisation: Microsoft (Africa Development Centre, Nairobi); Ministry of ICT (Kenya)
claims_extracted: Staff accounts (CIO Africa 12 Oct, tech-ish): Nairobi ADC employees were informed Monday 12 Oct 2026 that the centre closes; roles would end.
About 400 roles at risk per staff reports and media (WeeTracker 'nearly 400'; Kenyans.co.ke 400-500). Reported figure, NOT a Microsoft number.

Microsoft on-record response (obtained by CIO Africa and tech-ish, carried by Business Insider Africa 13 Oct): acknowledges 'proposed changes affecting its engineering operations in Kenya'; says it will continue operating in Kenya and supporting customers; neither confirms nor denies the closure; no headcount or dates given.

CS William Kabogo met a Microsoft delegation led by Jeff Bullwinkel (VP, Deputy General Counsel, Corporate) on 12 Oct; public X statement stresses 'retaining local talent, protecting jobs at Microsoft's Nairobi engineering centre and sustaining investor confidence'; meeting also covered AI adoption in government, digitisation, cybersecurity, digital infrastructure, digital skills, and Microsoft support for the National AI Policy.

Context: US$100M was the ADC launch investment target (five years, up to 500 engineers across Nairobi and Lagos), not a current valuation; second ADC site closure after Lagos (May 2024); ADC is a software-engineering hub, distinct from the stalled US$1B G42 campus (house record unchanged).
Same reporting names Oracle's September Nairobi cuts and fresh Kenyan job adverts for DC technicians and AI infrastructure sales - reallocation signal for the workforce tracker.
records.evidence_excerpt: Microsoft confirms proposed changes to Kenyan engineering operations as staff report a Nairobi hub closure plan and the government seeks to protect jobs (Business Insider Africa og:description, fetched 2026-10-14). Microsoft has acknowledged proposed changes affecting its engineering operations in Kenya. It says it will continue operating in the country and supporting customers. The company has not publicly specified the number of affected employees or when the changes would take effect.
